hypotheses.L: L(x)=sum_r x_r X_r, real symmetric X_r, x standard Gaussian
hypotheses.f: C1 increasing real function, f'>=c_R>0 on [-R,R]; assume displayed expectations finite. Bounded globally Lipschitz f suffices.

proof: Set Z=[L,H]=sum x_r Z_r, Z_r=[X_r,H]. Let V=sum_r ||Z_r||F^2=E||Z||F^2.
Wick expansion gives E||L Z||F^2 = ||sum_r X_r Z_r||F^2 + sum_rs ||X_r Z_s||F^2 + sum_rs <X_r Z_s,X_s Z_r>.

The first term is <=K V by the norm of the row operator [X_1 ... X_n]. The second is <=K V by sum X_r^2<=K I. The absolute value of the third is <= the second by Cauchy-Schwarz and swapping r,s. Thus E||LZ||F^2<=3KV. Applying the same argument to adjoints gives E||ZL||F^2<=3KV.

For the spectral projection P_large(L)=1_{|L|>R}, ||P_large Z||F^2<=R^-2||LZ||F^2 and ||Z P_large||F^2<=R^-2||ZL||F^2. Consequently the squared norm of the moderate/moderate block has expectation >=(1-6K/R^2)V=V/2.
In an eigenbasis of L, [f(L),H]_ij=f[lambda_i,lambda_j] Z_ij. Every divided difference is nonnegative, and it is >=c_R if both eigenvalues lie in [-R,R]. Hence E<Z,[f(L),H]> >=c_R V/2.
Cauchy-Schwarz gives the claim; V=0 is immediate.
simultaneous_axis_corollary: For mutually orthogonal rank-one projections P_i, sum_i ||[E,P_i]||F^2<=2||E||F^2 for every real matrix E, by direct entries in their common orthonormal basis.
If A=L+Y and f is globally Lipschitz with constant L_f, Frobenius functional-calculus Lipschitzness gives E||f(A)-f(L)||F^2<=L_f^2 E||Y||F^2.
Therefore sum_i E||[L,P_i]||F^2 <= (8/c_R^2) sum_i E||[f(A),P_i]||F^2 + (16 L_f^2/c_R^2) E||Y||F^2.
application: f(a)=q(a)/(1+q(a)) is bounded, increasing, globally Lipschitz and has positive derivative on every compact interval. Thus quantitative simultaneous axis diagonalization of bounded response transfers to coefficient off-axis energy when B is uniformly bounded.
limits: Does not provide a B operator bound from the weak source Omega penalty.
Does not prove the all-deficit entropy theorem or the global cubic rounding theorem.
No numerical test or finite sample is used as a proof.
